ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image shows an example figure made from nine light-blue congruent squares with dark borders. The squares are joined full side to full side in a connected stepped polyomino-like shape; there are 3 squares in the top row, 3 in the middle row, and 3 in the bottom row, offset from each other. Reasoning: Each square has side length 1 cm, so if the 9 squares were all separate, their total perimeter would be 9 × 4 = 36 cm. When two squares share a full side, that shared side is no longer on the outside boundary, so it reduces the total outside perimeter by 2 cm. Let e be the number of shared sides. Since the figure must be connected side-by-side, at least 8 shared sides are needed to connect 9 squares. To get the greatest perimeter, we minimize the number of shared sides, so e = 8. Therefore the maximum perimeter is 36 − 2 × 8 = 20 cm. This can be achieved by arranging the 9 squares in a chain, such as a straight row.

Then perimeter = 36 − 2 × 8 = 20 cm. A straight row or chain of 9 squares achieves this, so the greatest perimeter is 20 cm.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the displayed figure is one possible connected shape built from nine equal squares, with squares attached by full sides. From the text, there are 9 squares of side length 1 cm, and we need the maximum possible perimeter over all such figures. Build the figure one square at a time. The first square has perimeter 4 cm. Each new square must be placed side-by-side with the existing figure, so it shares at least one full side. Adding a square contributes 4 cm of its own boundary but the shared side removes 2 cm from the outer boundary, so the perimeter can increase by at most 2 cm per added square. After adding the remaining 8 squares, the perimeter is at most 4 + 8 × 2 = 20 cm. This upper bound is attainable by adding each new square so it touches the previous figure along exactly one side, for example in a straight line or non-touching chain. Therefore the greatest perimeter is 20 cm.
